title: Bind a near-unit Stein row to the rounded child at unchanged precision
body:
Bind PR6228's emitted p=3 near-unit Stein row to the unchanged PR4205 compensated rounded generator child. On the explicit padded rank-one example, **P shrinks from3I/2 to23I/16, but the scaled-G envelope grows6→48/7**. Both versions choose Gamma4 and the same25/77/71/69/49-bit allocation,98 layers and264 gates. A smaller coefficient-row norm alone does not imply a smaller child envelope or precision saving.

The wrapper executes the actual new producer, checks entrywise E/T reconstruction and the original receiver predicates, then runs both original child programs. Eight caller inputs and the single vendored normalizer remain byte-exact; frozen producer loading and rounding sites are unchanged. Pending PR6228 history is retained only for reproducible source pins; the diff from main contains this scoped package.

**Evidence:** Windows11 / CPython3.12.11 registered normal and optimized runs produce identical complete receipts:34 predeclared finite observations and6 rejecting controls. Each observation separates coefficient, arithmetic, total and source-return error, plus height/grid bounds. Metadata and committed-byte/source-history checks pass. Separate AI parameter/proof review found no remaining blocker.

**Transparent correction:** the initial claim paired a half-valued mixed input with incoming0. Root source review caught that incompatible input grid before registered acceptance. All17 inputs per arm were retained; both arms now use incoming1, with an explicit grid guard and a rejecting incoming0 control. Data49 still dominates, so allocated widths and plans are unchanged. This is recorded in TASK, receipt and [canonical Discussion](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19284117).

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/near-unit-rounded-child
python3 scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/near-unit-rounded-child --check-source-history
```

**Limits:** finite inputs do not prove arbitrary-input rounded correctness. This is the compensated generator child used by the Gaussian pipeline; the chosen matrix is not an actual Gaussian kernel. No Full/Gaussian/finite-core caller, physical delivery/setup tariff, new allocation proof or savings claim is supplied. No hostedCI, human/kernel acceptance or selected-frontier change is claimed.

Credit Nick Petalas/PR6228; Jose Manuel/PR4198/4205; Vlado Vojdanovski's macro; Chafik Boukhalfa's certified phases; Cinna Davis and retained caller/structured-matrix lineage. New adapter and finite comparison: AAAmirinu with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0.
